prompt: Which statement about a normal distribution is **false**?
options: It is symmetric about the mean.
The mean, median and mode are equal.
About 68% of values lie within one standard deviation of the mean.
All values lie within three standard deviations of the mean.
markscheme: **D.** The normal curve never touches the horizontal axis, so any value has non-zero probability density, but about 99.7% of values (not all) lie within 3 standard deviations. A, B and C are true.

prompt: Heights $H\sim N(170,\ 8^{2})$ cm. Sketch a normal curve and shade the region representing $P(160<H<180)$, labelling the mean and the values 160 and 180.
markscheme:
Bell-shaped curve centred at 170 **(A1)**; region between 160 and 180 shaded, symmetric about 170 **(A1)**

A sketch helps to check whether an answer should be more or less than 0.5.

prompt: Heights $H\sim N(170,\ 8^{2})$ cm. Find the height exceeded by the tallest 10% of people.
markscheme:
$P(H<h)=0.9$ **(M1)**; $h\approx180$ cm (180.3) **(A1)**

**Common mistake:** entering 0.1 as the left-tail area. The tallest 10% lie *above* $h$, so the area to the left is 0.9.

concept: The normal distribution as a model
prompt: Explain why the normal distribution is a reasonable model for adult heights but not for the number of goals scored in a football match.
markscheme: Heights are continuous and roughly symmetric about the mean; goals are discrete, small and skewed (many 0s and 1s, a long right tail) **(R1)**
